mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators are strong (PAYEMS growth > 0.3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 QoQ > 0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both FEDFUNDS and the 10-year Treasury yield (proxied by RSAFS) below their respective 5-year averages signals a collapse in long-term real interest rates, which boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and RSAFS both fall below 5-year averages simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation spikes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side slowdown, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong demand (GDPC1 growth > 0.4% QoQ).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month average by more than 10% signals a housing market rebound, which boosts construction-related equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when mortgage rates spike (implied from FEDFUNDS and RSAFS).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month averages signals a soft labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and UNRATE > 12-month MA in the same month
regime_hint: expansion with rising labor force participation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when wage growth accelerates (implied from labor cost data not available in catalog).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent FEDFUNDS rate held below 1% for more than 12 months in an environment of rising CPIAUCSL (> 2% YoY) signals a prolonged period of accommodative policy amid inflation, which erodes real yields and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for > 12 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.9%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%).
